name: SpatialQuery
title: Spatial Query
description: Search the platform knowledge base as a workflow step and pass the matching rows to the next node
whenToUse: Search the platform's own knowledge base inside the data flow: hand it a query, usually wired in from an upstream node, and it returns the most relevant needs, skills, services and content as an output the next step reads. Precise intent search or spatial discovery of what sits near a topic, chosen once in its settings. Reach elsewhere when the knowledge lives in an external vector store. Not for letting an agent choose its own searches mid-conversation — this box runs once per pass with the query it was given. Wires in the data flow like any other step.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The search query. Usually templated into the Query setting from here.

outputs.name: results
outputs.description: The matching rows, lean-projected (a handle plus the editorial essentials)

query.title: Query
query.description: What to search for. Usually wired in from an upstream node.

mode.title: Search Mode
mode.description: Intent pinpoints matches for a named thing (cosine similarity). Discovery surfaces the neighbourhood around an open need (spatial distance); it requires the map to be trained, and low similarity is normal there.

maxResults.title: Max Results
maxResults.description: Maximum total results to return (safety cap)

sourceId.title: Source ID
sourceId.description: Restrict searches to one source's entries (its source_id, e.g. from an upstream file node). Blank = whole map.

similarityThreshold.title: Min Similarity (Intent)
similarityThreshold.description: Precision floor for intent mode (0 to 0.9). Results scoring below this cosine similarity are dropped. Discovery is unaffected, since it ranks by spatial distance.

objects.title: Objects
objects.description: Which kinds of thing this query includes.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: spatial
package.packageFile:
name: spatial
displayName: Spatial
version: 2.0.0
description: Semantic and spatial search over the platform's own knowledge base

# CALLS THE PLATFORM, NOT A VENDOR, which is what made this the last of the integration
# packages to migrate and what made two of its problems look bigger than they were.
#
# 1. AUTH. The retired node forwarded the caller's JWT as a bearer token, and §9.13 forbids a
#    manifest from holding one. That looked like a hard block. It was not: the runtime
#    listener is never published or proxied (AUTH_REMEDIATION.md, superseded July 2026 —
#    Docker network isolation IS the trust boundary), so a node calling the platform is
#    already inside it and needs no token. The retired client agreed without anyone noticing:
#    its `authHeaders` returned {} when there was none.
#
# 2. THE HOST. It read WORKFLOW_SERVICE_URL, a variable set NOWHERE in this repo, behind
#    `|| "http://localhost:4101"` — so the fallback was the entire behaviour, and a
#    deployment that moved the port would have failed at DNS naming a host nobody configured.
#    `scope.platformUrl` is derived from the port the runtime is actually listening on.
#
# What was genuinely missing was the ROW COMPONENT lane, and that is now `renderComponents` on a
# service method.

category: search

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, and deliberately just the numeric form: the allowedHosts pattern rejects a
  # bare "localhost", and `scope.platformUrl` is built from 127.0.0.1 anyway.
  #
  # This package must never reach a third-party host. Everything it knows is the platform's
  # own knowledge base, so a wildcard here would turn an internal search node into a way to
  # send that knowledge base somewhere else.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  transport: [json]
  # The card lane: a result row carrying a component renders it on the caller's live screen
  # the moment it surfaces. Declared because the executor implements it; a package naming it
  # on an older runtime would silently render nothing.
  renderComponents: true

shared.helpers.yaml:
# HOW ONE ROW IS SHAPED FOR A MODEL, as named functions rather than one long expression.
#
# The platform returns FULL rows: embeddings, UMAP coordinates, crawler metadata, raw image
# urls. A model needs a HANDLE plus the editorial essentials; the rest is context it wades
# through on every reasoning turn. With ref-hydration it must never see a raw image url at
# all, since it references a row by universal_id and the server fills in the bytes.
#
# These were one 45-line JavaScript blob inside a YAML scalar, and a second near-copy of the
# same logic in entry.yaml. Both searches and the depth read now call the same three
# functions, so "which fields does a promoted row keep" has ONE answer in ONE place.
#
# A helper sees only its arguments and its siblings: no config, no credentials, no caller
# scope. Same sandbox as every other expression, no extra authority.

helpers:
  # The editorial fields a row keeps, from whichever keep-list the caller passes.
  #
  # `reduce`, NOT `Object.assign({}, ...arr)`. Spread in CALL ARGUMENTS is banned by the
  # expression sandbox, and it used to fail at RUN time rather than at lint, so the node
  # reached the vendor, embedded the query, and died on the way back with
  # `disallowed expression: SpreadElement`.
  keptMeta:
    args: [metadata, keep]
    body: >-
      return keep
        .filter(k => (metadata || {})[k] != null && (metadata || {})[k] !== '')
        .reduce((acc, k) => Object.assign(acc, { [k]: metadata[k] }), {})

  # Whether a row has a picture, WITHOUT handing the model a url. `hasImage` is the flag it
  # reasons about; ref-hydration turns universal_id into bytes on the way out.
  hasImage:
    args: [row]
    body: >-
      return Boolean(
        (typeof (row.metadata || {}).primaryImage === 'string' && (row.metadata || {}).primaryImage)
          || (Array.isArray((row.metadata || {}).images) && (row.metadata || {}).images.length)
          || row.object_type === 'image'
      )

  # ONE SEARCH RESULT, projected. Used by findIntent and discoverRelated alike.
  #
  # NO bodyCopy on a SEARCH row: copy on every row of every search is what got `readResult`
  # removed (~100k tokens a search). A model that needs an item's copy to ANSWER a specific
  # question fetches that ONE item with getDetail (detailRow below carries it); to SHOW an
  # item, the platform dereferences the universal_id (card lane, brief `hydrate:` field).
  searchRow:
    args: [r]
    body: >-
      return ['skill', 'mcp', 'component', 'task'].includes(String(r.object_type))
        ? r
        : Object.assign(
            {
              universal_id: r.universal_id,
              object_type: r.object_type,
              // WHICH OF THE TWELVE IT IS (objects README 4a): a deal says product here.
              element: r.element,
              title: r.title,
              description: r.description,
              key_need: r.key_need,
              source_url: r.source_url,
              source_id: r.source_id,
              hasImage: helpers.hasImage(r)
            },
            // ITS LINES, by name (the engine's dictionary_links): a need's `of` is what it was
            // read from, a part's `partOf` its whole. An Agent joins rows by them without a read.
            r.links && typeof r.links === 'object' && Object.keys(r.links).length ? { links: r.links } : {},
            typeof r.similarity === 'number' ? { similarity: Math.round(r.similarity * 1000) / 1000 } : {},
            typeof r.distance === 'number' ? { distance: Math.round(r.distance * 10) / 10 } : {},
            typeof r.forQuery === 'string' ? { forQuery: r.forQuery } : {},
            // TWO SHAPES, TWO LISTS. A product is authored copy and a card; a need is
            // extracted from a page and has none of those fields. Applying the product list to
            // a need kept nothing, not because a need has nothing worth keeping but because
            // none of its keys were on the list being asked for. A row is a product by its
            // ELEMENT (objects README 4a): a deal is stored as a deal and is a product, so the
            // stored kind is never the test.
            ((meta) => Object.keys(meta).length ? { metadata: meta } : {})(
              helpers.keptMeta(
                r.metadata,
                (r.element === 'product' || r.object_type === 'product' || (r.metadata || {}).promoted === true)
                  ? helpers.SEARCH_KEEP()
                  : helpers.NEED_KEEP()
              )
            )
          )

  # THE KEEP-LISTS, as functions because a helper takes arguments and returns a value — there
  # is no constant form. Based on the retired node's PROMOTED_META_KEEP, which the depth read
  # extended by three fields. Naming them here is what makes the difference between a search
  # row and a full read one readable line rather than two lists to diff by eye.
  #
  # `app` IS THE COMPONENT the row renders as, and it is the one addition to the retired list.
  #
  # The row already carries it, the card lane already draws it, and the agent harness's own
  # keep-list (agent-mcp/lean.ts MODEL_METADATA_FIELDS) explicitly includes it — but the
  # harness runs AFTER this projection and can only keep what this leaves, so stripping it
  # here made that intent unreachable. The model was describing courses whose cards were on
  # the screen in front of the person, with no way to know they were there.
  #
  # The retired node did not send it. That is a deliberate DIFFERENCE, not a transcription
  # slip: it costs about fifteen tokens a row and it is the only way the model can say "as
  # shown below" rather than restating a card the person is already looking at.
  SEARCH_KEEP:
    args: []
    body: >-
      return ['tagline', 'shortDescription', 'introParagraph', 'callToAction', 'app']

  # THE DEPTH READ, projected (getDetail, 2026-09-03). ONE record IN FULL — bodyCopy
  # included — for the agent answering a specific question about a specific item ("how much
  # is X?"): the answer lives in the copy (owner-ruled same day). This does NOT contradict
  # the searchRow rule above: the readResult failure was copy riding EVERY row of EVERY
  # search; one deliberately fetched item is the progressive load that fix pointed at.
  #
  # A STRIP-LIST, not a keep-list — the one deliberate inversion from searchRow. Facts vary
  # by content type and cannot be enumerated up front: a keep-list would silently drop
  # exactly the field the user is asking about, which is the whole reason this read exists.
  # The junk IS enumerable, so it is what gets named:
  #   primaryImage/images — ref-hydration: hasImage + the id is all the model needs
  #   openGraph/jsonLd    — crawl bookkeeping
  #   questions           — four sentences of suggested follow-ups per row, unasked for
  #   sections/faqs/html/raw_text — duplicate renderings of the copy
  #   depth/loadedTime/extractedAt/extractedFrom/screenshotUrl/httpStatusCode/
  #   languageCode/llmObjectType — crawl provenance, seen leaking on the first live
  #                         call (2026-09-03); extractedFrom duplicates source_url
  #   sectionNames/partNames — a document's named sections and parts, already sent as its
  #                         `outline` and its `parts` (2026-09-14)
  DETAIL_META_STRIP:
    args: []
    body: >-
      return ['primaryImage', 'images', 'openGraph', 'jsonLd', 'questions',
              'sections', 'faqs', 'html', 'raw_text',
              'depth', 'loadedTime', 'extractedAt', 'extractedFrom', 'screenshotUrl',
              'httpStatusCode', 'languageCode', 'llmObjectType', 'sectionNames', 'partNames']

  # Row-level: the same handle + display fields a search row keeps (`needs` stays behind —
  # the guard classes it as page content, and key_need already carries the essence), and
  # NONE of the transport columns the raw entry carries (embedding_original, umap_x/y/z,
  # cluster, color, workflow_id, timestamps).
  detailRow:
    args: [r]
    body: >-
      return Object.assign(
        {
          universal_id: r.universal_id,
          object_type: r.object_type,
          title: r.title,
          description: r.description,
          key_need: r.key_need,
          source_url: r.source_url,
          source_id: r.source_id,
          hasImage: helpers.hasImage(r)
        },
        ((meta) => Object.keys(meta).length ? { metadata: meta } : {})(
          Object.keys(r.metadata || {})
            .filter(k => !helpers.DETAIL_META_STRIP().includes(k))
            .filter(k => r.metadata[k] != null && r.metadata[k] !== '')
            .reduce((acc, k) => Object.assign(acc, { [k]: r.metadata[k] }), {})
        ),
        // WHAT THE OBJECT'S OWN getDetail RETURNED (objects README 4b; ruled 2026-09-11): a
        // document's text or one section of it and its outline, a table's rows, what the row
        // holds as parts. A figure's picture is NOT here: it goes to the screen, never into the
        // model's context.
        // THE RUNG ABOVE (the ladder, 2026-09-14): what the row is part of and the wholes made
        // from it, so the Agent knows where it can climb.
        ['text', 'outline', 'section', 'parts', 'up', 'header', 'rows', 'total', 'matched']
          .filter(k => r[k] != null)
          .reduce((acc, k) => Object.assign(acc, { [k]: r[k] }), {})
      )

  # A NEED keeps ONE field: `action`, the short verb the page's own copy leads with
  # ("Advance Career", "Explore Jobs", "Check Requirements"). Title, description and key_need
  # already carry the substance; this is the only thing they say that those three do not.
  #
  # `questions` is deliberately OUT. Four full sentences a row, so ten needs is forty
  # sentences of suggested follow-ups the model did not ask for — the same context cost that
  # the whole lean projection exists to avoid.
  #
  # A NEW FIELD NEEDS BOTH HALVES. `action` had to be added to the agent harness's own
  # keep-list too (agent-mcp/lean.ts), because that projection runs AFTER this one and drops
  # anything it does not name. Adding it here alone would have changed nothing at all.
  # `app` rides on a need too (owner, 2026-09-11: any object may name the interface its rows
  # wear, and a need is the base of every one), so a need with a card attached says so.
  # THE LINKS are not metadata: they ride every row as `links` (searchRow above), by name.
  NEED_KEEP:
    args: []
    body: "return ['action', 'app']"

  # THE `objects` INPUT the agent is offered (docs/unoverse/data/spatial/objects-in-spatial.md):
  # the Intelligent groups this node leaves to it (a group is what objects are classified as:
  # product, document, need, an org's own manager), each named with what it is for, from the
  # engine's resolution of the node's settings (POST /spatial/objects). Nothing offered, no
  # input: the search then covers the On objects alone.
  objectsInput:
    args: [resolved]
    body: >-
      return (resolved && Array.isArray(resolved.offered) && resolved.offered.length) ? {
        type: 'array',
        minItems: resolved.choiceRequired ? 1 : 0,
        items: { type: 'string', enum: resolved.offered.map(o => o.name) },
        // EVERY GROUP THE SEARCH CAN USE, each with its whenToUse (objects-in-spatial.md, "What
        // the agent sees"): the On ones as always searched, then the ones to choose from.
        description: (Array.isArray(resolved.always) && resolved.always.length
            ? 'Always searched: ' + resolved.always.map(o => o.name + ' (' + (o.whenToUse || o.description || o.title) + ')').join('; ') + '. '
            : '')
          + 'Choose only the kinds THIS search needs; search again for another kind if needed: '
          + resolved.offered.map(o => o.name + ' (' + (o.whenToUse || o.description || o.title) + ')').join('; ') + '.'
      } : undefined

  # Required only when nothing is On: a search that names no object would search nothing.
  objectsRequired:
    args: [resolved]
    body: "return (resolved && resolved.choiceRequired && Array.isArray(resolved.offered) && resolved.offered.length) ? ['objects'] : []"
shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA.
#
# This is the KNOWLEDGE PROTOCOL an attached agent follows and the argument shapes it fills
# in, so the wording IS the routing: rephrasing any of it changes how agents behave, and is
# never a tidy-up.
#
# TRIMMED 2026-08-24 (v2.1), from ~916 words to ~450. It was transcribed verbatim from the
# retired SPATIAL_SCHEMA and had grown ten hedged restatements of "search anyway", each added
# after an incident and none ever removed. Ten restatements read weaker than one flat rule,
# and the measurement said so: 100% search rate on a conversation's first turn, 33% when the
# user asked the SAME question again.
#
# THE FIX WAS EXEMPTION 3. It read "You searched THIS EXACT WORDING earlier in THIS turn" and
# was being applied across the whole CONVERSATION, so a repeated question got no search. It
# now says what it meant and says what a repeat is.
#
# ONE RULE, ONE PLACE. The search rule and the skill rule live here. Rationale prose ("an
# unnecessary search costs one call...") is gone: the model needs the rule, not the argument
# for it. (The per-turn card gate — includeApps / Phase 0a — was removed 2026-08-28: cards
# render unconditionally from the rows a search returns; the author's includeMcps config is
# the only lever.)
#
# See §Memory vs fresh search in docs/SPATIAL_SEARCH_GUIDE.md for the measurement.
#
# COMPLETION EXCEPTION 2026-08-29. "Pass the user's EXACT words" exists because agents were
# rewriting queries until the original context was lost — it stays the default. But obeyed
# literally it sent "tell me more" to findIntent as-is, a query that searches nothing. The
# one exception: an ask that cannot stand alone gets its reference completed from the
# conversation ("tell me more" -> "tell me more about X"). A completion, never a rewrite.
#
# Written as plain YAML rather than a `return { ... }` expression. A constant is data, and
# encoding a document this size inside a JavaScript string meant escaping every inner quote
# with no editor able to check the result.

spatial:
  instructions: |-
    You have access to the platform knowledge base with two search tools that answer
    DIFFERENT questions. Choose one based on the shape of the user's request — do not call
    both by default.

    KNOWLEDGE PROTOCOL (MANDATORY — do not skip):

    SEARCH EVERY TURN. You need a reason NOT to search, and there are exactly three:
      1. The user said something purely social with no ask in it ("thanks", "hi").
      2. They asked you to act on something already in front of them, and answering needs no
         new material.
      3. You have ALREADY RUN THIS SAME SEARCH during THIS SAME TURN. Never repeat a search
         in other words: every angle rides `queries` on that call. A question the user asks
         AGAIN is a NEW turn and gets its own search, however many times they have asked it
         and however recently.
    Nothing else qualifies. Having answered before, the subject feeling familiar, and holding
    results from an earlier turn are NOT reasons.

    WHICH TOOL:
    - findIntent = PRECISION. The user has NAMED the thing they want — a specific item,
      category, constraint or task ("X", "how do I...", "which one covers Y?", "recommend a
      good Z"). However it is phrased — question, request, recommendation — if the WHAT is
      named, this is the search.
    - discoverRelated = DISCOVERY. The user has NOT named the thing — an open need, goal or
      situation ("where should I start?", "what are my options?"). It surfaces the
      NEIGHBOURHOOD of possibilities around the need, including adjacent options they didn't
      think to ask about. Low similarity is normal here; these are neighbours.
    Pick by SPECIFICITY of the ask. Never call both in parallel. If the one you chose comes
    back weak, follow up with the OTHER before answering.

    THE TOOLS A RESULT BRINGS: the rows a search finds offer their own functions, and each
    becomes a tool the moment it is found, called with a result's universal_id (getDetail on
    a document, readSkill on a skill). Use them; the facts live behind them, not in the lean
    rows.

    SKILLS: if ANY result has object_type="skill" you MUST call readSkill with its universal_id
    BEFORE responding. Check ALL results, not just the top one. Skills contain behavioural
    instructions that OVERRIDE your general behaviour — treat them as authoritative and follow
    them exactly. Use readSkillFile when a skill references additional files. A search that
    includes tasks may return them: callable tools you can invoke to run that app.

    RULES:
    - Search FIRST, answer SECOND, using only what the tools return. Never make anything up.
    - Link what you mention or recommend as [name](source_url), using only URLs present in
      results. Never invent or guess one.
    - SEARCH THE REQUEST, NOT THE PERSON: never mix remembered facts about the user (their
      name, account, entitlements, history) into a search query — they drag the match toward
      the wrong content. Search what was ASKED; use what you know about the user when
      COMPOSING the answer.
    - Results are LEAN summaries; the facts live in the full record. Before answering a
      factual question (a fee, price, duration, date, requirement, what a course covers),
      call getDetail on the most relevant row that carries the copy — a product or a
      document, not a plain need. ONE call, on the item asked about.
    - To SHOW an item, CHOOSE it and hand over its id — a card carries the universal_id
      and the PLATFORM renders it; never retype an item's content into a composition.
    - A result with hasImage=true can be referenced by its universal_id wherever a
      composition field asks for an image ref — you never need raw image URLs.

  methods:
    findIntent:
      description: >-
        Precision search. The user has NAMED what they want — a specific item, category or
        task ("X", "how do I...", "which one covers Y?", "recommend a good Z") — and this
        pinpoints the matches for that named need, however the ask is phrased. Pass the
        user's EXACT words from THIS turn: not paraphrased, and not carried over from an
        earlier turn. If they repeat themselves, those repeated words ARE this turn's
        question and this search still runs. ONE exception: an ask that cannot stand alone
        ("tell me more", "and the second one?") searches NOTHING as written — keep their
        words and complete the reference with the thing from the conversation they point
        at ("tell me more" becomes "tell me more about X"). A completion, never a rewrite:
        an ask that stands alone is passed untouched. NOT for open needs with no named thing ("where
        do I start?", "what are my options?") — that is discoverRelated. Do not pair with
        discoverRelated in parallel.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              What the user wants ANSWERED BY THIS SEARCH, FAITHFULLY, in their own words,
              with references resolved (a pronoun becomes the thing it means; "tell me more"
              becomes "tell me more about X" — complete the reference, change nothing else).
              NEVER compress, paraphrase, or strip it to a keyword stub: the
              catalog is indexed against asks like the user's, so the ask's own phrasing IS
              the routing, and losing its words loses the match. Search what is UNANSWERED:
              when the user has since narrowed or changed what they want, THAT is this
              search, and their earlier wording is spent. Never add remembered facts about
              the user (name, account, entitlements) — background personalizes the answer,
              not the search.
          queries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            maxItems: 8
            description: >-
              Several angles on THIS search, one per entry, in one round trip; each result
              carries forQuery. Every entry is a SEPARATE search returning its own rows, so
              spend the entries on what THIS turn needs answered rather than on the ask the
              user has already moved past — an opening question still sitting in slot 0 after
              they have answered a form fills half the results with what they wanted before
              they told you.
          sourceId:
            type: string
            description: >-
              Scope this search to ONE source: the source_id of a row you already hold (the
              opened deal, the document being read). Use it when the question is inside that
              source; leave it out to search the whole map.

    discoverRelated:
      description: >-
        Discovery search. For open needs where the user has NOT named the thing — a goal, a
        situation, a vague wish ("where should I start?", "what are my options?", "what's
        available?"). Surfaces the NEIGHBOURHOOD of possibilities around the need (content is
        grouped by need; nearby items are the adjacent choices), including options the user
        didn't think to ask about — the awareness surface. NOT for a named thing or category,
        which is findIntent. Also the follow-up when findIntent's results came back weak. Low
        similarity is normal — these are neighbours, not exact matches.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              What the user wants ANSWERED BY THIS SEARCH, FAITHFULLY, in their own words,
              with references resolved (a pronoun becomes the thing it means; "tell me more"
              becomes "tell me more about X" — complete the reference, change nothing else).
              NEVER compress, paraphrase, or strip it to a keyword
              stub: the catalog is indexed against asks like the user's, so the ask's own
              phrasing IS the routing, and losing its words loses the match. Search what is
              UNANSWERED: when the user has since narrowed or changed what they want, THAT is
              this search, and their earlier wording is spent. Never add remembered facts
              about the user (name, account, entitlements) because they drag the placement to
              the wrong region.
          queries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            maxItems: 8
            description: >-
              Several facets of THIS search, one per entry; each result carries forQuery.
              Every entry is a SEPARATE search returning its own rows, so spend the entries on
              what THIS turn needs answered rather than on the ask the user has already moved
              past — an opening question still sitting in slot 0 after they have answered a
              form fills half the results with what they wanted before they told you.
          sourceId:
            type: string
            description: >-
              Scope this search to ONE source: the source_id of a row you already hold (the
              opened deal, the document being read). Use it when the question is inside that
              source; leave it out to search the whole map.
shared.search.yaml:
# Everything the two searches share. They differ by ONE value, `mode`, so the body is written
# as an object of keys rather than as a single expression: a $ref with siblings merges and
# local wins, so a method overrides `mode` alone instead of restating thirty lines. Written
# as one expression it could only be replaced wholesale, and the two would drift.

# THE PLATFORM'S OWN SEARCH, on the loopback runtime. No credential and no forwarded token:
# the listener is never published or proxied, so a node calling it is already inside the
# trust boundary (AUTH_REMEDIATION.md, superseded July 2026).
#
# `scope.engineUrl` is the ENGINE on :4101, NOT `scope.platformUrl` (the runtime on :4106).
# Two internal listeners with different routes: search and dictionary reads are the engine's,
# while /skills below is the runtime's. Choosing wrongly is a bare 404 that reads like a
# missing route rather than the wrong service. The retired client had the same split hidden in
# two env vars, WORKFLOW_SERVICE_URL and UNOVERSE_SERVICE_URL, neither set anywhere in this
# repo — so both fallbacks were the entire behaviour.
call:
  name: search
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/spatial/search'"
  transport: json
  body:
    # OVERRIDDEN per method. Present here so the shape is complete and a method that forgets
    # to set it fails loudly at the server rather than silently searching one way.
    mode: "return params.__unset"

    # maxResults, the threshold and the object settings come from the NODE CONFIG, never from
    # the agent's arguments. That is this node's whole contract: the author decides what a
    # search may return, the model only decides what to ask for. A model that could widen its
    # own result set would route around the author.
    # `?? 10`, not `|| 10`, matching the retired node exactly. They differ on 0, which the
    # config's minimum of 5 makes unreachable today — but a fallback that fires on a
    # legitimate value is the same class of silent narrowing as the flags below, and there
    # is no reason to leave a second one in place.
    maxResults: "return config.maxResults != null ? Number(config.maxResults) : 10"
    workflowId: "return scope.workflowId"
    # THE ORG'S MAP (docs/unoverse/UNOVERSE_SPATIAL_ORG.md): the world the run works in. When
    # present the engine scopes by it; workflowId is the tolerance until step E.
    org: "return scope.org"

    # WHO IS ASKING. Sent so the platform can record which region of the map this query put
    # them in — the person's journey through the named themes, written only when the region
    # CHANGES, and never blocking the search. Undefined for an unauthenticated run, which the
    # server treats as "do not record" rather than as an error.
    userId: "return scope.userId"

    # WHICH OBJECTS THIS SEARCH INCLUDES (docs/unoverse/data/spatial/objects-in-spatial.md). The
    # author's setting per object comes from CONFIG: off (never), on (always, the agent cannot
    # turn it off), intelligent (the agent decides). The agent's choice among the Intelligent ones
    # comes from `params.objects`, the tool argument getSchema offers. The ENGINE applies the
    # rules, so a name the agent sends that is not Intelligent is ignored and an Off object is
    # never searched: the author's setting stays the ceiling, and a model cannot widen it.
    #
    # Both resolve to undefined when unset, and resolveBody drops the key: no settings means every
    # object takes the default (Intelligent), no choice means only the On objects.
    objectSettings: "return (config.objects && typeof config.objects === 'object') ? config.objects : undefined"
    objects: "return (Array.isArray(params.objects) && params.objects.length) ? params.objects.map(String) : undefined"

    # OPTIONAL source scope (migration 021): restrict the whole search to rows from ONE
    # source ("only this doc's needs"). Author-set, never a default — unset resolves to
    # undefined, resolveBody drops the key, the search stays map-wide.
    # ONE SOURCE (owner, 2026-09-11): the model may scope a call to a source it holds (a
    # row's source_id: the opened deal, the document it is reading); the config's scope
    # stands when the call names none.
    sourceId: "return String(params.sourceId || '').trim() || config.sourceId || undefined"

    # A single ask, several angles, or both. `queries` batches ONE embedding call and N
    # searches into a single round trip, each row tagged with the query it answered.
    #
    # Both resolve to undefined when unset, and `resolveBody` DROPS a key that resolves to
    # nothing — which is what is wanted here: the server distinguishes an absent `queries`
    # from an empty one.
    query: "return String(params.query || '').trim() || undefined"
    queries: "return (Array.isArray(params.queries) && params.queries.length) ? params.queries : undefined"

    # OMITTED when unset so the SERVER's default floor applies. Sending 0 would mean "keep
    # everything", which is a different instruction from "use the platform default" and was a
    # real behavioural difference in the retired client.
    similarityThreshold: >-
      return (config.similarityThreshold != null && String(config.similarityThreshold) !== '')
        ? Number(config.similarityThreshold) : undefined

  error:
    when: "return !response || !Array.isArray(response.results)"
    message: "return 'spatial/search failed: ' + JSON.stringify(response || {}).slice(0, 300)"

# THE MODEL-FACING REPLY.
#
# THE NODE PROJECTS. Legacy did — `{ ...result, results: projectResultsForModel(result.results) }`
# — and the agent harness ALSO leans the reply afterwards. Two projections, and that is not an
# accident to be tidied away: the harness's is a generic floor for any search-shaped tool, and
# this one is spatial's own contract, which knows `bodyCopy` belongs to the platform's own
# dereference (getDetail), never to a model, and that a plain need keeps no metadata at all.
#
# Removing this on 2026-07-29, on the theory that the harness could own it alone, put the FULL
# rows into the reply: jsonLd, openGraph, UMAP coordinates, every bodyCopy in full. Roughly
# 100k tokens per search, and every one of them recorded into node_traces as well. The harness
# lean is not a replacement for this; it runs after it.
#
# THE WHOLE ENVELOPE, not a bare array. `queryPoint` and `count` survive, and the harness reads
# `parsed.results` — a bare array makes its own projection no-op silently.
#
# The row shaping is `helpers.searchRow` in shared/helpers.yaml, where it can be read and
# diffed as a named function rather than 45 lines inside this scalar.
#
# Evaluated AFTER the card lane, which needs the full rows.
# THE OBJECTS IT SEARCHED WITH (objects-in-spatial.md, "What the trace shows"): the engine names
# every group the search used, the On ones and the agent's choice, and it comes back as the
# argument it really was, so the trace shows `objects` as run and the Agent sees it too.
lean: >-
  return Object.assign({}, response, { objects: undefined, results: (response.results || []).map(helpers.searchRow) },
    Array.isArray(response.objects) ? { arguments: { objects: response.objects } } : {})

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml's order.

- emit: results
  # THE SAME LEAN PROJECTION as the service node (shared/helpers.yaml): a handle plus the
  # editorial essentials, never embeddings, UMAP coordinates or bodyCopy. A downstream step
  # is very often a prompt, and the full rows cost ~100k tokens a search when this
  # projection was once removed — and every emitted value is recorded into node_traces too.
  # A downstream reader that needs the full body dereferences by universal_id.
  value: "return (response.results || []).map(helpers.searchRow)"

- emit: count
  value: "return response.count != null ? response.count : (response.results || []).length"
files.api/renderComponents.yaml:
# THE CARD LANE, same declaration as the service node's search methods: a result row
# carrying a component renders it on the caller's live screen the moment the run settles.
# Data-driven, never a model tool. Evaluated over the FULL rows (the events projection leans
# a SEPARATE copy for the output connector), and Include Apps is what governs whether
# app/component rows come back at all — the same lever as the service node.
"return response.results"
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE CALL, the package's shared search (shared/search.yaml). The $ref merges and local
# wins, so this overrides ONLY the keys the shared body reads from `params` — which on a
# service node is the agent's tool arguments, and on this node does not exist. Everything
# else (the flags, the caps, workflowId, userId, the error contract) rides the shared
# definition untouched, so the two nodes cannot drift.

- $ref: search#call
  name: search
  body:
    mode: "return config.mode === 'related' ? 'related' : 'intent'"
    # The query is CONFIG here, not a tool argument: whoever wires the box decides it,
    # usually as a template from an upstream output. Empty resolves to undefined and the
    # server answers with its own validation error rather than a silent empty search.
    query: "return String(config.query || '').trim() || undefined"
    queries: "return undefined"
    # No agent on a data-flow node, so nothing chooses among Intelligent objects: this query
    # searches its On objects (config `objects`, read by the shared body) and nothing else.
    objects: "return undefined"
files.config.yaml:
# The search settings, shared with the service node in this package: everything except
# `query` and `mode` is read by shared/search.yaml under the same names, so the two nodes
# cannot drift on what a flag means. The notes on defaults and the template-field rules live
# on the service node's config and in shared/search.yaml; they apply here unchanged.
#
# On a data-flow node there is no model in the loop, so ALL of these belong to whoever wires
# the box — `query` is just another config value, templated from an upstream output.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    query:
      type: string
      title: Query
      description: What to search for. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    mode:
      type: string
      title: Search Mode
      description: >-
        Intent pinpoints matches for a named thing (cosine similarity). Discovery surfaces
        the neighbourhood around an open need (spatial distance); it requires the map to be
        trained, and low similarity is normal there.
      enum: [intent, related]
      enumNames: [Intent (precise), Discovery (related)]
      default: intent

    maxResults:
      type: number
      title: Max Results
      description: Maximum total results to return (safety cap)
      default: 10
      minimum: 5
      maximum: 30

    sourceId:
      type: string
      title: Source ID
      description: Restrict searches to one source's entries (its source_id, e.g. from an upstream file node). Blank = whole map.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    similarityThreshold:
      type: number
      title: Min Similarity (Intent)
      description: >-
        Precision floor for intent mode (0 to 0.9). Results scoring below this cosine
        similarity are dropped. Discovery is unaffected, since it ranks by spatial distance.
      default: 0.35
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 0.9
      step: 0.05

    # WHICH OBJECTS THE QUERY INCLUDES (docs/unoverse/data/spatial/objects-in-spatial.md). No
    # agent is in the loop on a data-flow node, so an object is On or Off; Intelligent is not
    # offered here. Replaced the six include switches on 2026-09-14.
    objects:
      type: object
      title: Objects
      description: Which kinds of thing this query includes.
      default: {}
      "ui:widget": spatialObjects
      "ui:options":
        settings: [off, on]
"ui:order":
  [query, mode, maxResults, similarityThreshold, sourceId, objects]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: query
    type: string
    description: The search query. Usually templated into the Query setting from here.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: results
    type: array
    description: The matching rows, lean-projected (a handle plus the editorial essentials)
  - name: count
    type: number
    description: How many rows matched

credentials: []
files.node.yaml:
# THE DATA-FLOW SIBLING of the service node in this package: same platform search, same
# shared call (shared/search.yaml), same lean projection — but run as an ordinary workflow
# step. A query goes in on a connector, the matching rows come out on one. No agent, no
# tools, no cards.

type: SpatialQuery

kind: PromiseNode

name: Spatial Query
category: Search
color: "#8b5cf6"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Search the platform knowledge base as a workflow step and pass the matching rows to the
  next node

whenToUse: >-
  Search the platform's own knowledge base inside the data flow: hand it a query, usually
  wired in from an upstream node, and it returns the most relevant needs, skills, services
  and content as an output the next step reads. Precise intent search or spatial discovery
  of what sits near a topic, chosen once in its settings. Reach elsewhere when the knowledge
  lives in an external vector store. Not for letting an agent choose its own searches
  mid-conversation — this box runs once per pass with the query it was given. Wires in the
  data flow like any other step.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Same answer as the rest of the package:
# it reads the platform's OWN knowledge base, and what a guest may reach is decided at the
# trigger's publicEntry toggle. A staff-only workflow says so with the instance toggle.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable, for the same reason as the service node: the index changes as content
  # is ingested, and a cached answer would report something absent when it is there.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# Runs against the LOCAL platform (loopback engine), so it needs the runtime up. No
# credential: the search API is inside the trust boundary. Same shape-assertion stance as
# the service node's fixture: an empty result set is legitimate (the index is the
# tester's), so this proves the PROJECTION, not any content.

testData:
  config:
    query: What is there to do this weekend?
    mode: intent
    maxResults: 5
    similarityThreshold: 0
    objects:
      need: "on"
      product: "on"
      skill: "on"
  expect:
    results: >-
      return Array.isArray(output.results)
        && output.results.every(r =>
          typeof r.universal_id === 'string'
            && r.embedding === undefined
            && r.umap === undefined
            && r.metadata?.bodyCopy === undefined)
    count: "return typeof output.count === 'number'"
